To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the complete four-dimensional Mueller matrix BRDF of a sinter PTFE reference sample for six incident angles and four wavelengths, and that we have developed a parameterization for the Mueller matrix data that is complete, obeys reciprocity, and is linear in wavelength.

the Mueller matrix BRD of sintered PTFE can be described by a phenomenological model, that the model is complete, and that it is a function of the scattering and incident angles, and that the model coefficients are a linear function of wavelength.

the Mueller matrix bidirectionally polarized reflectance distribution function for sintered polytetrofluoroethylene (sPTFE) can be described by a phenomenological parameterization, which includes the bidirectionally polarizied scattering modes and a linearization with respect to wavelength, that is complete, obeys all relevant reciprocity conditions, is accurate to within the experimental uncertainty, and is applicable over a wide range in incident and scattering directions and over the wavelength range from 351 to 106
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a complete and accurate model for the Mueller matrix bidrectional reflectance distribution function for a sintered PTFE sample.
the development of a phenomenological model for describing the bidirectional reflectance of a sinter polytetrafluoride material.
the measurement and modeling of the BRDF of a sinter PTFE material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Mueller matrix BRDS of the PTFE sample is fully described by the surface scattering model with the following parameterization: the surface scattering modes have a wavelength dependence that can be described as linear combinations of the wavelength dependence of the incident angle, the scattering angle, and the cosine of the scattering angle; and the coefficients in these combinations are wavelength-independent constants.

the PTFE sample is highly scattering, with a diffuse reflectance of 98.6% at 633 nm and 97.5% at 532 nm, and that its BRDF can be described as anisotropic, with a scattering mode parameter of 1.0 at 633 nm.
the Mueller matrix BRDT of sintered PTFE is a function of incident angle and wavelength, but not a function of scattering angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mueller matrix BRDT of a sinter PTFE sample can be described by a phenomenological parameterization that is linear in wavelength.
the phenomenological description of the Mueller-matrix BRDF of the sintered PTFE sample is a function of the incident angle, scattering angle, and wavelength.

we have measured the Mueller matrix BRDf for a sintered PTFE sample over the scattering sphere for six incident angles and for four wavelengths, and we have parameterized the data with a phenomenological model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single Mueller matrix BRDF model can be fit to the data for all six incident angles, four wavelengths, and 180° scattering angles.

the phenomenological description provides a complete description of the BRDF for a wide range of incident and scattering angles, and it can be extended to provide an on-demand description of reflectance for any combination of wavelength, incident, and scattering angles.
the Mueller matrix BRDT can be measured and described for arbitrary surfaces.
